properties.description: Action-conditioned JEPA pretraining on longitudinal ECG pairs with disease transitions as actions, evaluated by downstream diagnosis.
xResNet1d50 encoder and residual MLP latent predictor conditioned on a label-difference transition vector, with SIGReg, then evaluated as a classifier encoder.

properties.algorithm: xResNet1d50 encoder pretrained with action-conditioned latent prediction and SIGReg, then finetuned

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded from L0 to not_world_model because core persistent state (state.persistent) is only partial (assertion:B100:0019): pretraining pairs single waveforms (X_t, X_{t+1}) using the next recording's label difference a_t = y_{t+1} - y_t, and at inference the dynamics predictor is discarded so only a static single-ECG classifier encoder is evaluated (Tables 1-3). Next-latent prediction and action sensitivity are never evaluated; accordingly, the system is classed as a supporting component (not_world_model).

legacy_cells.B: Beyond Patient Invariance: Learning Cardiac Dynamics via Action-Conditioned JEPAs
legacy_cells.C: Jose Geraldo Fernandes; Luiz Facury; Pedro Robles Dutenhefner; Wagner Meira Jr.
legacy_cells.O: Circulatory diseases, including hypertension, ischemic heart disease, atrial fibrillation/flutter, and heart failure
legacy_cells.S: Does ECG-derived cardiac latent representation support multi-label diagnosis, including classification of a patient's first ECG for triage?
legacy_cells.T: Patients in MIMIC-IV-ECG with longitudinal ECG recordings and ICD-10 diagnoses; the dataset has 161,352 unique patients.
legacy_cells.V: Experimental multi-label cardiac diagnosis on a patient's first ECG (triage) and on all ECGs (monitoring).
legacy_cells.AJ: xResNet1d50 ECG encoder; three-layer MLP action projector; residual MLP latent-dynamics predictor
legacy_cells.AT: No filtering/update rule reported; each ECG is encoded to its latent state before next-state prediction.
legacy_cells.BD: Sparse per-diagnosis transition vector with entries −1 (resolution), 0 (stable), or 1 (onset); 76 cardiac clusters
legacy_cells.BL: Consecutive ECG-recording pairs (t to t+1); elapsed time between recordings is not an input.
legacy_cells.BT: Multi-label diagnosis classifier, evaluated with linear probing and fine-tuning
legacy_cells.BV: Latent prediction loss (squared distance between predicted and target next-state embeddings) plus SIGReg embedding-geometry regularization; downstream Asymmetric Loss for classification
legacy_cells.DQ: 800,035 ECG records; 161,352 unique patients; 638,683 consecutive ECG pairs
legacy_cells.EG: At 10% training data (approximately ~4k patients), reported triage AUROC was 0.69 for the dynamics model versus 0.64 for supervised learning; at 1%, the fine-tuned dynamics model reached 0.510 triage AUROC.
legacy_cells.EI: Supervised baseline: macro-AUROC 0.735 triage / 0.786 monitoring; naive patient-invariance SSL: 0.666 / 0.698 linear probe and 0.679 / 0.726 fine-tuned; ours: 0.725 / 0.744 linear probe and 0.742 / 0.786 fine-tuned (Table 1).
legacy_cells.EK: Compared SIGReg with VICReg (Table 3); compared linear probing with fine-tuning in the 1% data regime (Table 2).
legacy_cells.EL: At 1% data, full-parameter fine-tuning collapsed to near-random classification (triage AUROC 0.510); authors attribute it to adaptation gradients overwriting learned features.
legacy_cells.FB: ECG waveform encoded as a 256-dimensional latent cardiac/electrophysiological state; ICD-10 diagnosis-label transitions form a separate conditioning vector.
legacy_cells.FL: 12-lead ECG → xResNet1d50 encoder → 256-dimensional latent state; diagnosis-transition vector → MLP projector; residual MLP predicts the next latent state; a diagnosis classifier is trained/evaluated by linear probe or fine-tuning. No planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors propose LeJEPA-based action-conditioned latent cardiac dynamics, treating changes in diagnosis labels as transition vectors, and report downstream diagnosis performance and low-data sample-efficiency results.
legacy_cells.FN: On the full dataset, fine-tuned model macro-AUROC was 0.742 triage versus 0.735 supervised, and 0.786 monitoring versus 0.786 supervised. At 10% data, authors report approximately 0.69 versus 0.64 triage AUROC. At 1%, linear probing retained higher signal than fine-tuning (0.563 versus 0.510 triage AUROC).
legacy_cells.FO: Authors identify limitations: action vectors encode transition occurrence but not clinical magnitude; chronic conditions change slowly and yield weak transition signals; ICD-10 onset timing is ambiguous; the 1% fine-tuning regime collapses; only circulatory-system labels truncated to three digits are used.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors propose learned continuous action embeddings, conditioning on elapsed time, expanding labels to the full ICD-10 ontology, improving low-data learning, and future patient-specific counterfactual simulation.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors argue patient-invariance objectives can suppress transient disease signals and that existing physiological JEPA work is passive/autoregressive rather than explicitly conditioned on disease transitions.
legacy_cells.FR: The reported evaluation establishes downstream diagnosis representation performance, not direct future-state forecast accuracy, multi-step rollout fidelity, counterfactual validity, treatment-effect identification, planning/control, external validation, or prospective clinical benefit. The modeled actions are diagnosis-label transitions, not prescribed treatments.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M2 Encoders; M3 Belief-state service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose the learned representation through a modality encoder/state interface, then independently validate next-state prediction before using it for simulation or control.
legacy_cells.FU: Reviewer mapping (KB §20): Incomplete multimodal state construction
legacy_cells.FX: Full extracted PDF text, all 12 pages: title/abstract and introduction (pp. 1–2); related work (pp. 2–3); methods, equations, architecture, and Figure 1 (pp. 3–5); experiments/results and Tables 1–2 (pp. 5–7); conclusion, limitations, and future work (pp. 7–8); references (pp. 8–9); Appendix A dataset characterization and Figures 5–6 (pp. 10–11); Appendix B experimental setup and Table 3 (pp. 11–12). Tables and figures' extracted text were readable. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: No A:I workbook field is changed because no direct contradiction was found; E/F are supplied only because the PDF identifies the workshop venue/status and E was blank in the metadata. The demonstrated results are downstream diagnosis classification metrics, not direct dynamics-rollout or counterfactual validation. Disease-label transitions are modeled as actions but are not prescribed treatment actions and do not establish causal identification. The paper states code is on GitHub but supplies no exact repository URL in the extracted text. The M1–M10 blueprint module definitions referenced by the rubric were not among the declared inputs, so FS is omitted rather than guessed. No unreadable table or text extraction issue was observed. Evidence QA: 51/70 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (72.9%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 60 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 12 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. limitations: All 12 PDF pages were read as extracted text (including Appendix B, Figure 6, and Table 3 VICReg vs SIGReg ablation on p. 12), and rendered page images were visually inspected for pages 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, and 12 (Figs. 1-6, Tables 1-3).
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for B100 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass, no independent human review.
notes: The paper pretrains an xResNet1d50 ECG encoder with a JEPA-style next-latent predictor conditioned on a label-difference vector and SIGReg, then evaluates it for diagnosis. Finetuned macro-AUROC is 0.742 for Triage and 0.786 for Monitoring against 0.735 and 0.786 for supervised, with overlapping intervals on Triage. At 10 percent data, 0.69 versus 0.64 for supervised, and at 1 percent both collapse. Next-latent prediction and action sensitivity are not evaluated, and the dynamics model uses labels that the invariance baseline does not. Classified L0, supporting component, R2. Source points: action defined from the next label, label-use confound, overlapping intervals.
